title: The subjunctive in literary and formal prose: -ra and -se
summary: Hablara or hablase? The two imperfect subjunctives, where only -ra will do, long conditionals, and the fixed frames of formal prose: digan lo que digan, ¡quién pudiera!, que yo sepa.
focus: Using the -ra and -se subjunctive, the pluperfect subjunctive and fixed subjunctive frames in formal and literary Spanish
content:
## Two forms of one tense: -ra and -se

The imperfect subjunctive has two sets of endings on the same stem. The stem is the third person plural of the preterite minus **-ron** (hablaron gives habla-, fueron gives fue-, tuvieron gives tuvie-).

| | -ra | -se |
|---|---|---|
| yo | hablara | hablase |
| tú | hablaras | hablases |
| él / ella / usted | hablara | hablase |
| nosotros/as | habláramos | hablásemos |
| vosotros/as | hablarais | hablaseis |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | hablaran | hablasen |

In a subordinate clause they mean the same: **Me pidió que esperara** = **Me pidió que esperase**. The **-ra** form is the more frequent everywhere; **-se** is still used in Spain and in careful writing, and sounds bookish in much of Latin America. The pluperfect is **hubiera / hubiese + participle**.

## Where only -ra will do

Three uses belong to **-ra** alone:

- **Courtesy**: **quisiera**, **debiera**, **pudiera** soften a request or advice. *Quisiera hablar con la directora* (I would like to speak to the director). *Quisiese* is wrong here.
- **The press's past indicative**: **el que fuera ministro** = *el que había sido ministro* (the former minister). Common in journalism and literature, accepted in relative clauses, tiresome when overused. *-se* cannot do this.
- **The main clause of a conditional**: **Si lo hubiese sabido, no hubiera venido**, where **hubiera = habría**. Keep **-se** for the *si* clause.

## Long conditionals and the sequence of tenses

Formal prose builds long hypotheses with the pluperfect subjunctive:

- **Si la comisión hubiese aprobado el presupuesto, las obras habrían empezado en marzo.** (If the committee had approved the budget, the works would have begun in March.)
- **Si hubiera estudiado Derecho, hoy sería jueza.** (Past condition, present result.)

The tense of the main verb sets the tense of the subjunctive:

| main verb | subordinate |
|---|---|
| present, future, imperative: **pide, pedirá, pide** | present subjunctive: **que firme** |
| past or conditional: **pidió, pedía, pediría** | imperfect subjunctive: **que firmara / firmase** |

*El juez exigió que el testigo compareciera.* In much of Latin America the present survives after a past verb when the request is still pending (*pidió que firme mañana*); in formal Castilian prose, keep the sequence.

## Fixed frames: whatever, if only, as far as I know

- **Reduplication = "whatever"**: **digan lo que digan** (whatever they say), **sea como sea** (be that as it may), **pase lo que pase** (come what may), **vayas donde vayas**. In the past: **dijeran lo que dijeran**, **fuera como fuese**.
- **Wishes with ojalá**: present = still possible (**ojalá llueva**), imperfect = unlikely or contrary to fact (**ojalá lloviera**), pluperfect = too late (**ojalá hubiera llovido**).
- **¡Quién + subjunctive!** = if only I could: **¡Quién pudiera!**, **¡Quién lo hubiera dicho!** (Who would have thought it!)
- **Que yo sepa** = as far as I know. **Que digamos** after a negative = not exactly: *No es muy puntual que digamos.*

vocabulary.meaning: (that) I / he / she spoke: imperfect subjunctive, -ra and -se
vocabulary.example: La presidenta rogó al ponente que hablase más despacio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The chair asked the speaker to talk more slowly.

vocabulary.meaning: (that) I / he / she were or went: imperfect subjunctive of ser and ir
vocabulary.example: Aunque fuese domingo, la biblioteca seguía abierta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Even though it was Sunday, the library was still open.

vocabulary.example: Si hubiese llovido en abril, la cosecha se habría salvado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If it had rained in April, the harvest would have been saved.

vocabulary.meaning: I would like (courtesy; only the -ra form)
vocabulary.example: Quisiera hacerle una pregunta sobre el contrato.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I would like to ask you a question about the contract.

vocabulary.meaning: the former…, who had been… (press style, -ra as a past indicative)
vocabulary.example: La exposición homenajea a la que fuera directora del museo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The exhibition pays tribute to the woman who was once director of the museum.

vocabulary.example: Digan lo que digan las encuestas, el resultado está abierto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Whatever the polls say, the result is open.

vocabulary.meaning: be that as it may; one way or another
vocabulary.example: Sea como sea, el informe tiene que estar listo el lunes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: One way or another, the report has to be ready on Monday.

vocabulary.example: Pase lo que pase, te llamo esta noche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Whatever happens, I'll call you tonight.
If only we had booked a table.
A sabbatical year in Lisbon? If only I could!

vocabulary.example: Que yo sepa, nadie ha presentado una queja.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As far as I know, nobody has filed a complaint.

vocabulary.meaning: not exactly, hardly (after a negative, ironic)
vocabulary.example: El hotel no era barato que digamos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The hotel was not exactly cheap.

vocabulary.example: Se ruega a los asistentes que apaguen el móvil.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Attendees are kindly asked to switch off their phones.

vocabulary.meaning: even if, even though (+ subjunctive for a hypothesis)
vocabulary.example: Aunque me lo jurara, no lo creería.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Even if he swore it to me, I wouldn't believe it.

quiz.prompt: ___ hablar con la directora, si es posible.
quiz.explanation: Courtesy uses only the -ra form: quisiera softens the request like 'I would like'. Quisiese is not used this way.
hints: Polite requests belong to one of the two forms only.

quiz.prompt: Si lo ___ sabido antes, te habría avisado. (haber)
quiz.explanation: A past condition that did not happen takes the pluperfect subjunctive in the si clause: hubiera or hubiese sabido. Both forms are correct here.
hints: Imperfect subjunctive of haber, yo form.

quiz.prompt: La presidenta le rogó que ___ más despacio. (hablar)
quiz.explanation: Rogó is a past verb of request, so the subordinate takes the imperfect subjunctive: hablara or hablase.
hints: A past main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence uses -ra as a past indicative, the press style that -se cannot copy?
options: El que fuera alcalde de la ciudad inauguró la feria.
Si fuera alcalde, cambiaría las normas.
Aunque fuera alcalde, no lo votaría.
quiz.correct_answer: El que fuera alcalde de la ciudad inauguró la feria.
quiz.explanation: El que fuera alcalde means 'the man who had been mayor': -ra stands for había sido. The other two are ordinary subjunctives, where fuese would also work.
hints: Which fuera could you replace with había sido?

quiz.prompt: Digan lo que ___, no pienso cambiar de opinión.
quiz.explanation: The concessive frame repeats the same subjunctive: digan lo que digan = whatever they say.

quiz.prompt: Sea como ___, el plazo termina el viernes.
quiz.explanation: Sea como sea (be that as it may) repeats the present subjunctive. The indicative breaks the frame.
hints: The frame repeats the same form.

quiz.prompt: — Me voy a vivir un año a una isla. — ¡Qué envidia! ___
quiz.explanation: ¡Quién + imperfect subjunctive! expresses a wish you cannot fulfil: if only I could!
hints: A wish that is out of reach takes the imperfect subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá ___ salido antes; ahora hay un atasco enorme. (haber, nosotros)
quiz.explanation: Regret about the past (too late now) takes ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive: ojalá hubiéramos / hubiésemos salido antes.
hints: It is too late, so use the pluperfect subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Aunque me lo ___, no te creería. (jurar, tú)
quiz.explanation: A hypothesis with aunque and a conditional in the main clause takes the imperfect subjunctive: aunque me lo juraras / jurases.

quiz.prompt: El nuevo jefe no es muy simpático ___.
quiz.explanation: After a negative, que digamos at the end means 'not exactly': he is not exactly friendly. Digamos que ('let's say that') introduces a clause, so it cannot close the sentence, and pase lo que pase ('whatever happens') makes no sense here.

listening.meaning: I would like to ask you a favour.

listening.text: Pase lo que pase, firmaremos mañana.
listening.meaning: Whatever happens, we will sign tomorrow.

listening.text: Que yo sepa, el archivo abre los sábados.
listening.meaning: As far as I know, the archive opens on Saturdays.
listening.note: New word: el archivo = the archive.

listening.text: Ojalá el tren no se retrasara tanto.
listening.meaning: If only the train weren't so late.
listening.note: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive: contrary to fact.

listening.text: La alcaldesa pidió que se respetase el silencio en la sala.
listening.meaning: The mayor asked for silence to be respected in the hall.

listening.text: Si hubiésemos leído la letra pequeña, no estaríamos aquí.
listening.meaning: If we had read the small print, we wouldn't be here.
listening.note: New word: la letra pequeña = the small print.

listening.text: El edificio, que fuera cárcel en otro siglo, hoy es una biblioteca.
listening.meaning: The building, which had been a prison in another century, is a library today.
listening.note: -ra as a past indicative: que fuera = que había sido.

listening.text: Dijeran lo que dijeran los críticos, la novela se vendió muy bien.
listening.meaning: Whatever the critics said, the novel sold very well.
listening.note: New word: los críticos = the critics.

guide.tip: Test for the press -ra: if you can swap it for había + participle, -se is not an option.

conversations.title: The last read before printing
conversations.scenario: Elena, an editor, and Tomás, a copy editor, go through a novel's proofs the day before it goes to the printer.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Tomás, quisiera comentarte algo del manuscrito antes de que lo mandes a imprenta.
lines.meaning: Tomás, I'd like to mention something about the manuscript before you send it to the printer.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Dime. Que yo sepa, ya está todo corregido.
lines.meaning: Go on. As far as I know, everything has been corrected.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Casi. La autora alterna hubiese y hubiera en la misma página.
lines.meaning: Almost. The author alternates hubiese and hubiera on the same page.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Eso no es un error. En la oración con si valen las dos formas.
lines.meaning: That's not a mistake. In the si clause both forms are fine.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ya, pero aquí escribe: si lo hubiese sabido, no hubiese venido. Chirría.
lines.meaning: Sure, but here she writes: si lo hubiese sabido, no hubiese venido. It grates.
lines.note: In the main clause, hubiera or habría.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Tienes razón. En la principal mejor hubiera, o mejor aún, habría.
lines.meaning: You're right. In the main clause, hubiera is better, or better still, habría.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Y en la contracubierta habla del que fuera su editor. ¿Lo dejamos?
lines.meaning: And on the back cover she mentions the man who was once her editor. Do we leave it?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Es estilo de prensa, pero es correcto. Digan lo que digan los puristas.
lines.meaning: It's press style, but it's correct. Whatever the purists say.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: De acuerdo. Ojalá todos los textos llegaran tan limpios.
lines.meaning: Fine. If only all texts arrived this clean.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Quién pudiera! El próximo trae trescientas páginas y ni una coma.
lines.meaning: If only! The next one has three hundred pages and not a single comma.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sea como sea, lo leemos juntos el lunes.
lines.meaning: Be that as it may, we'll read it together on Monday.

bites.title: -ra or -se
bites.rule: The imperfect subjunctive has two endings on one stem (hablaron gives habla-): hablara or hablase. In a subordinate clause they are interchangeable.
bites.example: Me pidió que esperase un momento.
bites.example_meaning: She asked me to wait a moment.

bites.title: Only -ra
bites.rule: Courtesy (quisiera), the press's past indicative (el que fuera ministro) and the main clause of a conditional (hubiera = habría) take -ra, never -se.
bites.example_meaning: I would like to see the director.

bites.title: Whatever, come what may
bites.rule: Repeat the subjunctive around lo que, como or donde to say 'whatever': digan lo que digan, sea como sea, vayas donde vayas.
bites.example: Vayas donde vayas, llévate un paraguas.
bites.example_meaning: Wherever you go, take an umbrella.

bites.title: Three wishes
bites.rule: Ojalá + present = still possible; + imperfect = unlikely or untrue now; + pluperfect = too late. ¡Quién pudiera! = if only I could.
bites.example_meaning: If only I had accepted that job.

sorts.title: Both forms, or only -ra?
sorts.why: In ordinary subordinate clauses both forms work; courtesy, the press's past indicative and the main clause of a conditional take -ra only.

items.text: Si lo hubiese sabido, no ___ venido

sorts.title: Possible, unlikely or too late?
sorts.why: Ojalá + present looks ahead to something possible; + imperfect wishes for what is not so; + pluperfect regrets the past.

spots.sentence: Quisiese hablar con el director, por favor.
El juez exigió ayer que el testigo comparezca.
spots.why: A past main verb about a past event takes the imperfect subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Digan lo que dicen, no cambiaré de opinión.
spots.why: The concessive frame repeats the same subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Si lo hubiese sabido, te lo habré dicho.
spots.why: The result of a past unreal condition is the conditional perfect: habría (or hubiera) dicho.

spots.sentence: No es muy simpático que digo.
spots.why: The fixed ironic tag is que digamos.

builds.meaning: I would like to speak to the director.

builds.text: Pase lo que pase, te llamaré.
builds.meaning: Whatever happens, I will call you.

builds.text: Si hubiese llegado antes, lo habría visto.
builds.meaning: If I had arrived earlier, I would have seen him.

builds.text: Que yo sepa, la tienda está cerrada.
builds.meaning: As far as I know, the shop is closed.
